chapter: The war years: Barnet, Hot Lips Page, Newton and Kirby
title: Touring Caribbean bases for the USO
summary: The unit toured Guantanamo, British and Dutch Guiana and Trinidad by helicopter and plane, entertaining troops across the British-owned Caribbean.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: But you mentioned this...where you were supposed to go to rehearse, but then you went to Cuba. Did you?
Well, what did you go to Cuba with?
In Cuba... I mean, I was with this show...

We toured by helicopter and everything else. Due to the War... We had bauxite mines all the way down to South America, and we had bases naturally down there. We stayed up at Guantanamo. Guantanamo is in Cuba, and that was our headquarters. We'd go to St. Julien and (?) and (?) if I have to name them... But one was at Atkinson Field in British Guyana; it was not Guyana, it was British Guyana. And then Zeinweg(?) Field was in Dutch Guyana. And that's about as far I went. We didn't go to the Cape of Good Hope.

And Zeinweg(?) Field was... Well, the ...(?). ... was the ...(?). ... And that was the jump-off place for the invasion of the American troops into Iran. General Patch(?) was the commanding General in the Caribbean theatre of war. Under his command...
Yeah, we played for all the bases. We played the bases in the Caribbean, which were mostly English. We didn't see American troops for quite a while, until we got

to Trinidad. We were playing for Australians and Great Britain in the Grand Cayman Islands. This is where you began to see how much of the Caribbean the British own. They have thousands of islands there; and it's not on the Rand-McNally map, but on the military maps. I mean, you've got the Pincairn and then you've got the Exumas, the Greater Exumas and the Lesser Exumas, the Great Antilles and the Lesser Antilles, you know.

There are islands there that... We entertained in places that I went to that for generations English families and others... Not only English, but Danish and... Of course, if Leif Ericcson would have turned south, everybody would have been speaking Norwegian! But there are farms and plantations, and they have their own water supplies, and then their communication would be through...say, twice a year a boat might visit their island or something like that.
